description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of data sources within the combined training set, as referenced in the paper “Automatic Evaluation of Attribution by Large Language Models.” It visually breaks down the proportional contribution of each dataset across 12 distinct categories. The largest segment is NQ (Natural Questions), occupying 31.3% of the total and rendered in blue. The second-largest is FEVER at 16.1% (teal), followed by SNLI at 15.4% (orange), and VITAMINC at 13.0% (light blue). MULTINLI contributes 11.3% (pink), while XSUMHUL accounts for 1.6% (light purple). Smaller contributions come from ANLI (4.6%, dark orange), FACTCC (2.6%, yellow-green), ENTFA (1.8%, green), SCITAIL (1.2%, olive), PUBHEALTH (0.5%, dark teal), and MULTIFC (0.5%, dark red). Each slice is labeled with its dataset name and percentage, connected via thin gray lines to avoid clutter, and the segments are arranged in roughly descending order clockwise from the top. No legend is present, as labels are directly annotated on the chart. The visual emphasizes the dominance of NQ and the long tail of smaller datasets.
